intent: I've been eyeing those gorgeous Damascus-looking chef's knives that sell for way under a hundred and sit at nearly five stars. But whenever knife people talk about them, someone sneers that the wavy pattern is just laser-etched onto soft steel and the edge folds in a month. So who's right, the thousands of happy buyers or the snobs? I'd love to understand what real Damascus or layered steel even is, whether it matters for how a knife holds an edge, and whether any of these pretty affordable knives are secretly fine. If not, what should my money go to instead?

intent_v1_legacy: I got completely sucked into a documentary about plastic in the ocean and now I'm curious how we even got here. Can you take me through the whole arc, from when plastics first showed up early last century, through the explosion of single-use stuff in the 1950s, the environmental pushback in the 70s, and all the regulation and awareness in the decades since?
